context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

What do you do?

"Indeed, they do not. Which is why it has been posted for three days without a single party taking it." He taps the paper, the ink still fresh. "The Sheridans are paying for the ore that stopped coming. But this job—it is listed as *investigate* the village and find out what happened, not clear it out. Belle does not move from the tavern arch, her brown eyes narrow and calculating as she studies the stranger who has dared to approach her. "A party, he says," she mutters, her voice low and rough like grinding stones. "Better than rat-catching, sure enough. But Wendhope is far as fuck." She looks him over, from boots to pauldrons, and for a moment it seems as like she is sizing him up as if he were a piece of meat.
Then, a slow grin spreads across her face, all teeth. "You got any idea how much coin that will cost us to get there?"

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: The Sheridans pay the travel, Belle, it's in the posting. Dalan? You've been reading the same notice for ten minutes. Bow, sword and axe. Sounds like a party to me.

context.name: Dalan
context.text:
Dalan's pointed ears twitch at the sound of his name, and he glances up from the posting with wide, green eyes. A small, pink blush colours his cheeks as he shifts his weight from one foot to the other, and he seems to hesitate.
"I... I suppose so," he says, his voice soft and polite. "I have been registered at the Guild for a year now, but I have not yet found a party that... that is." He trails off, his eyes darting between the stranger and Belle, and then back to the and notice. "If you wish to take the posting, I would be happy to join you." He seems almost nervous, but there is a light in his eyes—a quiet determination that betrays a his shyness.
He adjusts the strap of his wooden longbow over his shoulder and looks back at the stranger. "My name is Dalan Evergreen. I am a Ranger."

context.name: Belle
context.text: Belle's eyes flick between the elf and the stranger, and then she gives a short, sharp laugh. "A Ranger and a... what are you, then?" She asks the stranger, her hand resting on the pommel of Cleaver's stone head. "We're taking the posting, then. I'll handle the front line. Ranger gets the shots. You do the rest." She looks back at them, her grin widening. "Now let's see if this party's got any fucking teeth."

context.name: Ellie
context.text: Ellie's eyebrows rise slightly, and she sets her pen down with a measured click. "The Ash Lanterns," she repeats softly, her blue eyes flicking between the three of you, as if trying to picture it. "That is a fine name." A small, genuine smile touches her lips before she picks up her pen again and writes it in the Guild's register. "The Ash Lanterns, taking the Wendhope investigation." Her handwriting is elegant and precise. "You're all F-rank, so your rewards will be D-rank standard, plus the Sheridan travel stipend." She pauses, then looks up at you. "We'll have that ready for you when you return. I hope to see you all again."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Thank you, Ellie. Right, Ash Lanterns: market for rope, lanterns and a week of rations, then the north gate before noon.

context.name: Belle
context.text: Belle pushes off from the tavern arch, and for the moment, the grin has vanished from her face. She looks at the party—at Max, at Dalan—with brown eyes that seem to be sizing them up as if they were a pack of hounds. "Right. Rations, rope, and lanterns. We'll pick those up as we go. The north gate is far." She looks at you, her hand resting on Cleaver's pommel. "And I hope this party has any fucking teeth."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Once we're past the city fields I fall in beside Dalan. So, a year between parties. What went wrong with the last ones?

context.name: Dalan
context.text:
Dalan's ears twitch, and he looks up with wide green eyes, surprised that anyone is talking to him. He seems to hesitate for a moment, his hand gripping the strap of his bow.
"I... I have not had many parties," he admits softly, his gaze falling to the path. "They did not... they did not want me. They said I was not strong enough. That I was too soft to fight." He looks back at Max, a flicker of something passing through his expression. "They did not see me shoot."
His voice is quiet, but there is a quiet determination in it. "I have been registered for a year. I have not yet had a chance to prove myself."

The wind picks up as dusk settles over the clearing, and the light is turning amber. The trees are shadows and the road is a dark ribbon between them. The horse is restless in your hold.

She looks at you, her expression grim. "You take the first watch. I'll be second. Dalan gets the dawn." She gives a short, sharp nod and looks to the forest. "And if anything comes out of those trees, we'll be ready."

The fire is small and controlled, and its light is barely enough to keep the darkness away. The Sheridan horse is quiet, its hooves softly shifting in the dirt. The forest is silent around you, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold and carries the scent of pine and old earth.

The horse is quiet. And the fire is dying.
But the road is still there, and the carriage is still there, and there is no sign of anyone coming.
The only sound is the crackle of the fire, and the distant howl of a wolf or something like it, and the soft shift of the horse’s hooves.
What do you do?

The road is empty, and the mists are thick, and the horse is still quiet.

She looks at the horse, then back at the road. "Wendhope is far. We'll need to get there before the sun gets too high."

A stone wall, a ring of houses, and the pit-heads and ore carts of a mining village.
Wendhope.
It sits in the valley, and there is no smoke from the fires, and there are no people in the streets. And there is nothing that moves, or shifts, or stirs, in the quiet of the morning.
What do you do?

line: I step back and look up at the wall walk. Dalan, do you see anyone up there? I call out again: we have food and bandages, we only want to talk.

replies.speaker: Dalan
replies.text:
Dalan steps forward beside Max, and his pointed ears twitch as he glances up at the wall. His eyes are wide and focused, and for a long moment, he is silent. Then he speaks, his voice low and soft.
"I... I see nothing," he admits, his gaze scanning the battlements again and again. "Nobody is moving up there." He looks back at Max, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Is that possible? That a whole village is just... empty?"

replies.speaker: Belle
replies.text: Belle's brown eyes narrow and she looks at the empty road. "A whole village empty? Fuck that." She spits on the ground and looks at the gate. "Something is wrong. And it ain't natural." She looks back at Dalan. "Get your bow ready. I can't shake the feeling that we're not alone out here."

"I... I see nothing," he admits, his gaze scanning the battlements again and again. "Nobody is moving up there." He looks back at Max, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Is that possible? That a whole village is just... empty?"

context.name: Belle
context.text: Belle's brown eyes narrow and she looks at the empty road. "A whole village empty? Fuck that." She spits on the ground and looks at the gate. "Something is wrong. And it ain't natural." She looks back at Dalan. "Get your bow ready. I can't shake the feeling that we're not alone out here."

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
The wind is cold and carries the scent of pine and damp earth, and the forest is silent around you. The village sits in the valley below, and there is no smoke from the fires, and there is nothing moving in the streets.
And there is only the sound of your voice, and the knock, and the silence that follows.
And there is the horse, and the carriage, and the empty road, and the absence of people.
The only movement in the village is the fluttering of a tattered cloth tied to one of the buildings, and the distant rustle of leaves in the wind.
And the horse is quiet. And the silence is thick.
What do you do?

context.name: Note
context.text: ◈ Hold, Wendhope Is Closed — Get inside Wendhope before sundown.

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text: Three bows come up on the parapet at once. "That's far enough!" The archer in the middle has a scar over his left eye and has not slept in days. "Wendhope's not taking visitors. Turn round now and you'll make the crossroads by sundown."
